newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 96/7 underlying budget def A$4.9bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 96/7 underlying budget def A$4.9bln.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that the preliminary underlying budget deficit for 1996/97 to June 30 was A$4.934 billion compared with A$10.317 billion in 1995/96.
The preliminary headline budget surplus was A$2.514 billion compared with a deficit of A$5.043 billion in 1995/96, he said.

Underlying outlays for 1996/97 were three percent above 1995/96 while revenue collections were 7.7 percent higher, mainly due to a rise in income tax collections, higher quarterly provisional tax instalments, higher debit on assessment receipts and lower provisional tax variations.

Companies tax, superannuation (pension) funds tax, and petroleum resource rent tax also contributed to the higher revenue collections during the year. Growth in revenue was partly offset by a large one-off payment of interest withholding tax recieved in April 1996 and lower interest receipts on state and territory debt. Company tax collections were 4.7 percent higher than forecast in the May budget.

"This is mainly due to higher than expected payments from previously non-taxable companies, and larger than expected receipts from large early December-balancing companies," a statement released by Costello said.
Other individuals' tax collections were 4.4 percent or A$500 million higher than estimated in May compared with a boost of A$853 million in company tax collections during the year.

The statement said individual tax collections rose due to lower than anticipated provisional tax variations and consequently higher than expected provisional tax collections and stronger than expected balance of assessments.
In the May budget the government forecast an underlying budget deficit of A$6.856 billion for 1996/97. The forecast for the headline balance was for a surplus of A$764 million.
The preliminary headline budget surplus of A$2.514 billion comprised headline outlays of A$128.51 billion and revenue of A$131.02 billion.

The statement said headline outlays grew 1.4 percent in 1996/97, mainly in areas of social security and welfare, general purpose inter-government transactions (mainly reflecting lower state debt repayments and a one-off settlement payment made to Victoria).
The increase in welfare outlays came from higher disability support pensions, sole parent pensions, family payments, the government's family tax initiative and its "new-start" employment allowance.

This growth in outlays was partially offset by the receipt of proceeds from the sale of The Commonwealth Bank of Australia, a special payment received from Telstra, and a reduction in labour and employment outlays.
The increase in revenue of 7.7 percent compared with a 7.0 percent increase budgeted for the year.
The rise in headline outlays of 1.4 percent compared with a budgeted increase of 2.4 percent.
